title: Prefill Sequencer: weighted split policy to trade latency vs throughput
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: The current prefill->decode handoff places whole requests into monolithic phases which causes two bad outcomes under load: (1) short, latency-sensitive requests suffer head-of-line delay when long prefills monopolize slots; (2) long requests fragment throughput because they prevent optimal kernel packing. Goal: design and prototype a Sequencer-based "weighted split" policy that probabilistically slices prefill work into micro-windows sized by utility (latency benefit * kernel packing score), and schedules them across two hedged queues: fast-path (latency SLO) and bulk-path (throughput-optimized). The Sequencer will use dynamic weights derived from per-route SLO, historical kernel-selection efficiency (measured in effective tokens/sec), request urgency, and customer tier. Integration must emit per-request telemetry for attribution and allow runtime feature flags for alpha experiments.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype scheduler that splits requests into micro-windows with configurable min/max window sizes
End-to-end experiment showing >=20% p95 latency reduction for latency-tier routes under 75% load with <=5% throughput regression for bulk routes
Telemetry pipeline emits per-window attributes: kernel_hints, queue_assigned, split_fraction, parent_key
Config-driven weights and thresholds exposed via console feature flag and runtime config
Automated unit tests and integration smoke test against local runtime harness
notes: Design rationale: blending probabilistic splitting reduces deterministic starvation patterns seen with rigid phase-splitting
Window sizing heuristic: utility = alpha * latency_importance + beta * kernel_efficiency_score; alpha adjusted by route SLO and beta by recent kernel packing stats
Hedged queues: fast-path capacity reserved via a token-bucket governed by latency headroom estimator; bulk-path performs larger micro-batches and prefers quantized kernels
Kernel hinting: sequencer will annotate windows with preferred kernel hints (FP16/INT8, attention-optimized kernel) to improve packing runtime acceptance
Fallback behavior: if fast-path is saturated, windows are either reweighted to bulk-path or hedged with a small replica on fast-path for critical requests
